name: Maintenance labor and skills gap
why_it_matters: Fewer experienced technicians and vibration analysts per machine
qualitative_justification: Weak tightening. Deloitte/Manufacturing Institute project 1.9M unfilled manufacturing jobs by 2033 (2024 study; 2.4M by 2028 in the 2018 study), but those are manufacturing-wide. For industrial machinery mechanics (49-9041), BLS employment rose from 250,810 (2006) to 412,650 (2023) while the real median wage was flat (+0.2%/yr, C09). Shortage claims are not visible in the wage data. Sources: labor_facts_D.csv, points.csv C09.

name: Data interoperability standards (OPC UA, MQTT/Sparkplug, IO-Link, MTConnect)
why_it_matters: Getting machine data out of mixed-vendor plants
qualitative_justification: Significant loosening, not a removed hard barrier. OPC UA reached IEC 62541 status (E002), gained PubSub with MQTT transport in 2018 (E004) and MQTT 5 in 2023 (E005); FX v1.0 (E006) and its 2025 certification program (E007) extend to field level; OPC 40001 Machinery building blocks and process values (E008, E009) and umati's ~25 published machinery companion specs (E016) give shared semantics; Sparkplug 3.0 (E015) and MTConnect (E012, E010) cover MQTT and machine-tool niches; OPC membership passed 1,000 in 2024 (E011). Held at 2 because no condition-monitoring-specific companion spec, ISO/IEC 20237 recognition of Sparkplug, IO-Link node counts or shipped-product numbers were confirmed (E015, E017 notes), and several competing stacks remain.

name: Condition-monitoring and prognostics standards (ISO 20816, 17359, 13381, 55000)
why_it_matters: Shared vocabulary and thresholds buyers can cite
qualitative_justification: Minor loosening: an incremental refresh of an existing voluntary framework rather than a new enabling standard. ISO 17359 is at its 2018 third edition (E019, E020, E021); the ISO 10816/7919 family was consolidated into ISO 20816 (E022-E025) with edition 2 of Part 1 under publication in Oct 2026 (E026) and Part 3 under revision (E027); ISO 13373 gained machine-specific parts through 2026 (E028, E029); ISO 13374 data-flow architecture dates from 2003-2015 (E030); ISO 13379-1 and ISO 13381-1 prognostics were re-issued in 2025 (E031, E032, E033); ISO 55000 second edition 2024 (E034, E035); ISO 18436 certification parts continue (E036). Nothing new in 2023-2026 creates a PdM-specific data model, and no IEC/IEEE PdM standard (IEC TR 63283 series, IEEE 1856) could be verified, so this is a coverage gap.

name: Machine data access law (EU Data Act, right to repair)
why_it_matters: Whether third parties can legally read machine data
qualitative_justification: Significant loosening for access to machine data, mostly in the EU. The Data Act applies since 12 Sep 2025 (E039) and covers industrial and agricultural machinery as connected products (E038); the design-for-access obligation for products placed on the market after 12 Sep 2026 is already in effect (E040); unfair-terms rules reach older long-term contracts from 12 Sep 2027 (E041). Offsetting factors: raw/pre-processed data only, a no-compete clause on the data, and the pending Digital Omnibus (E042) which could add trade-secret refusal grounds. The EU repair directive (E043, E044) is consumer-oriented. US state laws largely exclude industrial equipment (Minnesota E047; Colorado E045 covers agriculture only; E046), and the Deere settlement (E048) is agricultural, proposed and not yet confirmed as entered. UK (E049) unconfirmed for industrial scope. India, China, Japan, New York, California and Argentina were not verified.

name: Machinery, AI and cyber compliance (EU Machinery Reg, AI Act, CRA)
why_it_matters: Compliance cost and liability for connected, AI-driven machines
qualitative_justification: Significant tightening (compliance cost and design obligations), partly softened by delay. CRA reporting under Art. 14 applies since 11 Sep 2026 (E061), with full application 11 Dec 2027 (E062) and Chapter IV from 11 Jun 2026 (E060); Machinery Regulation applies 20 Jan 2027 (E050, E051); NIS2 transposition is overdue in several states (E063); IEC 62443 is the de facto technical route (E064). AI Act: general application 2 Aug 2026 (E056), but Reg. 2026/1744, in force 27 Jul 2026 (E052), moved Annex III high-risk to 2 Dec 2027 (E057) and Annex I to 2 Aug 2028 (E058) and carved machinery out of direct high-risk rules, so the AI hurdle for PdM is smaller than before. Scored 2 not 3: no new hard prohibition on PdM, most obligations hit hardware makers (sensors, gateways, machine builders) more than analytics vendors, and the scope of each law for PdM software was not verified. US CIRCIA final rule has no effective date (E065).

name: Early predictive-maintenance patents
why_it_matters: Expiring or lapsed core patents free up methods
qualitative_justification: Only a few generic prognosis/diagnosis patents with 2005-2008 filings were confirmed (F001-F004), all expiring roughly 2025-2027; two more (F005-F006, priority 2006/filed 2009-2010) lapsed early for unpaid fees per Google labels; earlier prior art already expired 2020-2023 (F007-F009). No evidence found that any of these actually blocked entrants; no Lens/Espacenet access, citation ranking not done.

name: Chip supply and trade barriers
why_it_matters: MEMS and MCU availability, lead times, tariffs
qualitative_justification: Component shortage eased (record 26.6 weeks Mar 2022, F010-F012; flat-to-falling at 27 weeks by Jun 2022 and forecast to fall in 2023, F013-F014) while US-China tariffs and controls tightened (F015-F016, F019, F022) then partly loosened (F020-F021, F023-F024). Net effect on industrial sensors/MCUs not isolated; Z2Data and mature-node tariff coverage not verified.

name: Scarcity of labeled failure data
why_it_matters: Few plants have enough run-to-failure examples to train on
qualitative_justification: Public bearing/engine datasets exist since 2008 (F026-F034) and simulation/GAN approaches are emerging (F035), but all are small (e.g. 17 bearings in PRONOSTIA, F030) and authors still report failure data as scarce (F030, F034, F036). No cross-company data-sharing initiative found.

name: ML capability for anomaly detection and prognostics
why_it_matters: TinyML, unsupervised detection, time-series foundation models, LLM copilots
qualitative_justification: Embedded ML runtimes fit in KBs (F037) and open pre-trained time-series models appeared in 2024 (F038-F040), but benchmarks are generic forecasting/anomaly sets with mixed wins (MOMENT loses on VUS-ROC to k-NN); no machinery-specific benchmark evidence. 2019 TinyML/Edge Impulse launches, Chronos and LLM maintenance copilots were not verified and have no rows.

name: OEM control of machine data and service contracts
why_it_matters: Who owns the data and the service relationship
qualitative_justification: Legal and standards openness advanced: OPC UA (F041), EU Data Act applying 2025-09-12 with connected-product design duty from 2026-09-12 (F045), Gaia-X/Catena-X/OI4 (F042-F044) while OEM service bundling persisted (F046). Provisional: Data Act provisions on third-party sharing and OEM contract clauses not verified; Catena-X is automotive, not machine PdM.

name: Proof of ROI and buyer trust
why_it_matters: Evidence that prediction pays, and insurer or auditor acceptance
qualitative_justification: Adoption evidence is thin: PwC 2017 found 11% at PdM 4.0 maturity (F047-F048); IoT Analytics 2023 claims 95% positive ROI among adopters but discloses no method (F049) and also says many solutions under 50% accuracy (F050). No insurer acceptance or independent ROI study obtained.
